title: Discrimination and health

draft.title: Discrimination and health
card: Discrimination is unfair treatment of people because of a trait such as gender, ethnicity or disability.
It can block access to education, work and health care. For example, girls may be kept out of school, or a person with a disability may be refused a job.
Less education and work can mean lower income. Reduced access to health care can mean illnesses go untreated.
Groups that face discrimination can therefore have poorer health and less opportunity to develop. Fair access helps reduce these gaps.
draft.remember: Discrimination can block access to education, work and health care, which harms health and development.

a.q: What is discrimination, as it affects health and development?
opts: Unfair treatment based on gender, ethnicity or disability
Differences in income that arise from personal choices
A lack of clean water in a particular region
Treatment that is the same for every person
a.why: Discrimination is unfair treatment because of a trait such as gender, ethnicity or disability. A lack of clean water is a different factor, because it is about services, not about how people are treated.
a.clue: Focus on unfair treatment linked to who a person is.

b.q: In a country where clinics turn away women unless a male relative comes with them, how might health be affected?
opts: Women may get less health care, so illness goes untreated
Men will have less access to health care than women
Women will have better access to education and work
All families will have equal access to health care
b.why: The rule blocks women's access to care, so illnesses can go untreated and health can worsen. The rule is aimed at women, so it does not reduce access for men. The case is about health care, not education.
b.clue: Who is being blocked, and from what service?

a.best: Unfair treatment based on gender, ethnicity or disability

b.best: Women may get less health care, so illness goes untreated

problems.detail: The right option is the only one with a qualifier ('may'), while the others use 'will' or 'All'. It is also the longest, so a student could pick it without knowing the idea.

a.q: What is discrimination, as it affects health and development?
opts: Unfair treatment based on gender, ethnicity or disability
Differences in income that arise from personal choices
A shortage of clean water and toilets in a region
Treating every person the same, whatever their traits
a.why: Discrimination is unfair treatment because of a trait such as gender, ethnicity or disability. A shortage of clean water is a different factor, because it is about services, not about how people are treated.
a.clue: Focus on unfair treatment linked to who a person is.

b.q: In a country where clinics turn away women unless a male relative comes with them, how might health be affected?
opts: Women may get less care, and illness may go untreated
Women may get better care, as relatives check on them
Men may lose access to care, as clinics favour women
Everyone may get equal care, as one rule covers all
b.why: The rule is a barrier: a woman without a male relative is turned away, so she may miss care and her illness may go untreated. It does not improve women's care, and it does not limit men's access, because the rule is aimed only at women.
b.clue: Who is being blocked, and from what service?
